question: One mole of Aluminium Sulphate Al₂(SO₄)₃ contains:
solution:
The correct answer is __**12 moles of oxygen atoms**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• One mole of Aluminium Sulphate Al₂(SO₄)₃ contains **12 moles of oxygen atoms**.
 
• To determine this, we analyze the chemical formula Al₂(SO₄)₃.
 
• Each sulphate ion (SO₄²⁻) contains 4 oxygen atoms.
 
• In Al₂(SO₄)₃, there are 3 sulphate ions.
 
• Thus, the total number of oxygen atoms is calculated as 3 (sulphate ions) × 4 (oxygen atoms per sulphate ion) = 12 oxygen atoms.
 
• This matches the provided answer of **12 moles of oxygen atoms** in one mole of Aluminium Sulphate.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Aluminium Sulphate is commonly used in water purification, paper manufacturing, and as a mordant in dyeing and printing textiles.
 
• It is also used in the food industry as a firming agent.
 
• The molecular weight of Aluminium Sulphate Al₂(SO₄)₃ is approximately 342.15 g/mol.
 
• When dissolved in water, it dissociates into aluminium ions (Al³⁺) and sulphate ions (SO₄²⁻).
